intro: Kettering is the Dayton metro's most populous suburb, and its homes are aging all at once: 85.5% of homes were built before 1980 and the median home dates to 1961. The city itself documents creek water flooding into basements along Little Beaver Creek and Little Sugar Creek, with home flood damage recorded in 1959 and 1973. Its defense-housing layers — Greenmont Village (1941–42) and the Van Buren Apartments (1951–53) — add some of the metro's oldest fast-build stock, and its 1950s–60s ranches carry the finished-basement retrofit trap: living space added decades after the build, over silted drain tile and lidless sump pits.
